candidates.title: Unqualified lettered option back-reference across documents that each own their own a/b/c list
candidates.cause: A cross-document back-reference cites bare option letters (e.g. "the (b)/(c) refutations") without naming which document's list owns them. When both documents independently letter their options a/b/c, a reader in document order binds the letters to the WRONG list — the one they have already read — and concludes that a still-live decision was already refuted, closing an open task as unactionable. The failure is silent: both documents are internally consistent and correct, so nothing is wrong to find in either one; the defect exists only in the unqualified reference between them, and it bites hardest when the ambiguous citation PRECEDES the live mandate in document order. Remedy: scope every cross-document letter to its owning list, and add the reciprocal clause at the cited-from site so the disambiguation works from either entry point.
candidates.evidence_quote: `plans/reify-flag-marker-backlog-rca-2026-07-22.md` §6a.3's ADDENDUM 2026-08-17 closes with "Full ruling, dated census and the (b)/(c) refutations: `docs/flag-marker-sweep-recurring.md` §"Decision (task 3923)"." Those (b)/(c) are the linked document's own list, about the retired `--check` gate. But §5 of the SAME document owns an unrelated "Optional hardening" a/b/c whose b and c are the two edits carried by task 2917 (measured `pending`), and §6a.5 records that mandate — three lines AFTER the ambiguous citation. A reader going top to bottom meets the "refutations" first and concludes 2917's ratified work was already refuted. The same bullet's earlier "retired (option a)" is the same collision: that "a" is the linked document's, while §6a.5's "Option a" is §5's. Filed as esc-2917-2 by task 2917's architect.
